questions.problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=-{x}^{2}+3yz$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,u+v,\,{v}^{2}⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{8{v}^{2}+1}.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{8{v}^{2}+1}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(-{x}^{2}+3yz)\,{|}_{x=u\,y=u+v\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =-(u\cdot u)+3\cdot (u+v)\cdot ({v}^{2}) \\  & =-{u}^{2}+3(u+v){v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(-{u}^{2}+3(u+v){v}^{2})\sqrt{8{v}^{2}+1}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=xyz$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,uv⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & v \\ 0 & 1 & u\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & v \\ 1 & u\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & v \\ 0 & u\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-v,\,-u,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-v,\,-u,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(-v)^{2}+(-u)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(xyz)\,{|}_{x=u\,y=v\,z=uv} \\  & =u\cdot v\cdot uv \\  & ={u}^{2}{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,{u}^{2}{v}^{2}\sqrt{{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}+1}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=x-{y}^{2}z$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨uv,\,-u,\,-{v}^{2}⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨v,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,0,\,-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ v & -1 & 0 \\ u & 0 & -2v\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2v\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}v & 0 \\ u & -2v\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}v & -1 \\ u & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2v,\,2{v}^{2},\,u⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨2v,\,2{v}^{2},\,u⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(2v)^{2}+(2{v}^{2})^{2}+(u)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}+4{v}^{4}+{u}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(x-{y}^{2}z)\,{|}_{x=uv\,y=-u\,z=-{v}^{2}} \\  & =uv-(-u)^{2}\cdot -{v}^{2} \\  & =uv+{u}^{2}{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(uv+{u}^{2}{v}^{2})\sqrt{4{v}^{2}+4{v}^{4}+{u}^{2}}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=-x-y-z$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,{v}^{2}-{u}^{2},\,u⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}-{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-2u,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}-{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -2u & 1 \\ 0 & 2v & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}-2u & 1 \\ 2v & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -2u \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u,\,0,\,2v⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-2v,\,0,\,2v⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(-2v)^{2}+(0)^{2}+(2v)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}+4{v}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8}v.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(-x-y-z)\,{|}_{x=u\,y={v}^{2}-{u}^{2}\,z=u} \\  & =-u-({v}^{2}-{u}^{2})-u \\  & ={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}-2u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}-{v}^{2}-2u)\sqrt{8}v\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces
questions.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}({x}^{2}-{z}^{2})\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=2u+v,\,y=2u-2v,\,z=u+2v
$$

for $-1\le u\le 1$ and $1\le v\le 2.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u+v,\,2u-2v,\,u+2v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u-2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u-2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,-3,\,-6⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨6,\,-3,\,-6⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36+9+36} \\  & =\sqrt{81} \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & ={x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,{|}_{x=2u+v\,y=2u-2v\,z=u+2v} \\  & =(2u+v)^{2}-(u+2v)^{2} \\  & =3{u}^{2}-3{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,1\le v\le 2},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(3{u}^{2}-3{v}^{2})\cdot 9\,\text{d}A \\  & =9{∬}_{D}\,(3{u}^{2}-3{v}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =9{\int }_{1}^{2}({\int }_{-1}^{1}(3{u}^{2}-3{v}^{2})\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =9{\int }_{1}^{2}{[{u}^{3}-3{v}^{2}u]}_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =9{\int }_{1}^{2}(2-6{v}^{2})\text{d}v \\  & =9\cdot [2v-2{v}^{3}]_{1}^{2} \\  & =9\cdot (-12) \\  & =-108.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}(xy+z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=u+v,\,y=u-v,\,z=0
$$

for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le 2.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,u-v,\,0⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,-2⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨0,\,0,\,-2⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+0+4} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =xy+z\,{|}_{x=u+v\,y=u-v\,z=0} \\  & =(u+v)(u-v) \\  & ={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}(xy+z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\cdot 2\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}({\int }_{0}^{1}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{{u}^{3}}{3}-{v}^{2}u]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{1}{3}-{v}^{2})\text{d}v \\  & =2{[\frac{v}{3}-\frac{{v}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =2[\frac{2}{3}-\frac{8}{3}] \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}(x+2y-z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u-v,\,2u+2v,\,2v⟩
$$

 
over the domain $D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=6.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=6.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(x+2y-z)\,{|}_{x=u-v\,y=2u+2v\,z=2v} \\  & =(u-v)+2(2u+2v)-(2v) \\  & =5u+v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(5u+v)\cdot 6\,\text{d}A \\  & =6{∬}_{D}\,(5u+v)\,\text{d}A \\  & =6{\int }_{0}^{2}({\int }_{0}^{1}(5u+v)\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =6{\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{5{u}^{2}}{2}+vu]}_{0}^{1}\text{d}v \\  & =6{\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{5}{2}+v)\text{d}v \\  & =6{[\frac{5v}{2}+\frac{{v}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =6[5+2] \\  & =42.\end{aligned}
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =2xz\,{|}_{x=u\,y=u+v\,z=2v} \\  & =2u(2v) \\  & =4uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 2},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}2xz\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,4uv\cdot 3\,\text{d}A \\  & =3{∬}_{D}\,4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{2}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =3\cdot [{u}^{2}]_{0}^{2}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =3\cdot 4\cdot 4 \\  & =48.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}6xyz\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,u+v,\,v⟩
$$

 
over the domain $D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{3}.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{3}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =6xyz\,{|}_{x=u\,y=u+v\,z=v} \\  & =6(u)(u+v)(v) \\  & =6({u}^{2}v+u{v}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,6({u}^{2}v+u{v}^{2})\cdot \sqrt{3}\,\text{d}A \\  & =6\sqrt{3}{∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}v+u{v}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =6\sqrt{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}({\int }_{0}^{1}({u}^{2}v+u{v}^{2})\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =6\sqrt{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{{u}^{3}v}{3}+\frac{{u}^{2}{v}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =6\sqrt{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{v}{3}+\frac{{v}^{2}}{2})\,\text{d}v \\  & =6\sqrt{3}{[\frac{{v}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{v}^{3}}{6}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =6\sqrt{3}(\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065891/assets/6ad2702c610c5e7d31d07584c6e605467ff25c8474befd433214451169cc1180.png)
Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z) = z-y$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle u^2, \: -v, \: v \big\rangle
$$

for $(u,v) \in D \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2,$ where $u \geq 0.$ What is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that $\| \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v \| = 2\sqrt{2}u.$*
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S f(x,y,z) \, \textrm{d}S 
=
\iint\limits_D f(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \left\|  \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v \right\|  \text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
\| \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v \| = 2\sqrt{2}u.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(z-y)\,{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=-v\,z=v} \\  & =v-(-v) \\  & =2v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,4\sqrt{2}uv\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
\iint\limits_{S} (x-y)\: \textrm{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x = u+v, \qquad 
y = u-v, \qquad 
z = v
$$

for $0 \leq u \leq 3$ and $0 \leq v \leq 3.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S f(x,y,z) \, \textrm{d}S 
=
\iint\limits_D f(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \left\|  \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v \right\|  \text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u+v, \: u-v, \: v\right\rangle.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,-2⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨1,\,-1,\,-2⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+4} \\  & =\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =x-y\,{|}_{x=u+v\,y=u-v\,z=v} \\  & =(u+v)-(u-v) \\  & =2v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D = \{ (u,v) \: : \: 0 \leq u \leq 3, \: 0 \leq v \leq 3\},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}(x-y)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2v\sqrt{6}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{6}{∬}_{D}\,2v\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{6}{\int }_{0}^{3}2v\,\text{d}v\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}1\,\text{d}u \\  & =\sqrt{6}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{3}\cdot [u]_{0}^{3} \\  & =\sqrt{6}\cdot 9\cdot 3 \\  & =27\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
